buyBody: A fifty-unit run for America's 250th. High-MOI mallet, twin navy fangs for alignment, a soft white face insert and a red clover stamped where your eyes go. They are gone.

four.v: And that was the whole run

whatYouGet: One Tracer LGP02 Patriot putter, right hand
No headcover — none of our clubs ship with one
clubHeadline: Fifty of them, for a birthday that only happens once.
clubParas: Most putters are built to disappear into a bag. This one was built to get talked about on the first tee, and it is a limited drop for America's 250th — fifty units, and then nothing.

Under the paint it is the LGP02: a high-MOI mallet, stable through impact and forgiving on the strikes you do not center. The twin fangs are navy and they line up dead square, which is the entire reason fangs exist.
The face insert is soft and white, so the roll comes off quieter than the standard mallet, and the Lucky clover is stamped in red exactly where you look when you are over the ball.
It is sold out. It was always going to be.

clubSpecs.v: Red Lucky clover, in the eyeline.
Anyone who wanted one in July and moved fast enough.

videoBrief: 16:9, 30–40s. This is a collector's item more than a performance club, so shoot it as an object: rotating on black, fangs and clover catching light, serial detail if there is one.
specHeadline: A colorway, and a very short run.
specSub: Shared geometry with the standard LGP02. What is different is the alignment, the insert and the fact that there were only ever fifty.

specTabs.aside: Shopify's description for this club is a launch announcement rather than a spec sheet. The standard LGP02's figures are not copied across — the head is shaped differently.

look.photo: Bold, full-bleed, portrait. Navy fangs and the red clover against green, low sun. This is the most photogenic club in the range and the shot should treat it as an object rather than as equipment.
look.headline: Built to be noticed, and then to be gone
paras: Fifty units is not a marketing number, it is the whole production run. Everything about the club — the navy, the red clover, the white insert — was decided on the basis that it would never be restocked.
If you have one, that is the point of it.
look.aside: Everyone else is carrying the same putter with someone else's name on it. It's better to be lucky.

closeBody: The Patriot was $229, right hand, fifty made. Sold out — the standard Tracer Mallet is the one still available.
